inference_correction.user_hypothesis: Kamil pyramids differed from Giza and gold sealed in glass may be remnants.
inference_correction.admitted_consequence_of_prior_gate: IF a Kamil pyramid/operator existed in the project model, it cannot simply reuse the frozen Giza orientation and still explain LOVE/EDEM pointing.
not_admitted: that a pyramid or engineered pyramid-like structure existed at Kamil
that Kamil impact glass is melted architectural material
that gold in Kamil glass would by itself indicate a pyramid or Osiris technology

impact_glass.white_glass: Mostly SiO2 target melt, inclusion-poor, <0.1 wt% projectile contamination from Ni/Co systematics.
impact_glass.dark_glass: Mixed target-projectile melt containing shocked sandstone, diaplectic/lechatelierite glass, Fe-Ni metal blebs and rare projectile fragments; estimated 11-12 wt% projectile contamination.
impact_glass.physical_interpretation: Metal sealed in glass is already a documented natural Kamil impact product.

gebel_kamil_meteorite_bulk_metal.important_result: Gold is genuinely present in the impactor metal, but only at trace concentration, not as reported macroscopic gold objects.

gold_mass_scale.warning: Siderophile-element fractionation during explosive melting is documented at Kamil, so these are mixture-scale expectations, not exact predictions.

anthropogenic_gold_discriminator.natural_baseline: Trace Au correlated with meteoritic Ni-Co-Pt-Ir signatures and irregular impact-metal blebs.
anthropogenic_gold_discriminator.candidate_anthropogenic_signature: Gold-rich inclusion many orders above the meteoritic ~ppm baseline, worked morphology or alloying pattern, repeated geometric placement, and/or archaeological context independent of the impact melt.
best_non_destructive_methods: SEM-EDS for morphology and major-element context
LA-ICP-MS or micro-PIXE/ICP-MS where permitted for Au-Pt-Ir-Ni-Co ratios
micro-CT before sectioning to locate high-density inclusions
anthropogenic_gold_discriminator.collection_rule: Prefer already curated Kamil impactites and meteorite specimens; no field disturbance or collecting is required for this gate.

chronology.importance: The best-supported Kamil age interval overlaps the New Kingdom/Third Intermediate Period and includes the 13th century BCE.

bia_n_pet.appearance: The composite expression becomes clearly attested around the late 18th/19th Dynasty, about 1300 BCE, and thereafter can denote iron generally.

karnak_same_period.scholarly_note: Comelli et al. 2016 explicitly note that a Karnak text from the same period has been interpreted as probably describing a meteorite (citing Kitchen 1975).

seti_I_karnak_shooting_star_metaphor.textual_motif: The king is compared with a shooting star scattering fire/flame.

older_iron_sky_cosmology_control.finding: Modern Egyptological work argues that the association of bjA/iron with the sky, meteors and a celestial iron container is already present in Old Kingdom Pyramid Text traditions, much earlier than the likely Kamil event.
older_iron_sky_cosmology_control.consequence: Kamil cannot be used as the origin of all Egyptian iron-sky concepts merely because biA-n-pt becomes explicit around 1300 BCE.

reverse_pass.result: Remove pyramid semantics: Kamil already contains natural Fe-Ni metal blebs and projectile fragments sealed in impact glass.
Because the impactor contains Au=1.57 ppm, trace gold in projectile-contaminated dark glass is a natural prediction even with zero archaeology.
Therefore finding only trace Au in dark glass would NOT discriminate an engineered-gold hypothesis from ordinary impact mixing.
A real archaeological discriminator would require anomalously concentrated/worked gold or patterned high-density inclusions inconsistent with meteoritic mixing.

The textual gate is more interesting chronologically: Kamil's preferred 1600-400 BCE interval overlaps the ~1300 BCE emergence of explicit 'iron of the sky' terminology and a same-period Karnak meteorite interpretation.
Earlier Pyramid Text iron-sky imagery prevents promotion of this overlap to a claim that Kamil created the concept; no securely identified ancient record of the Kamil event is currently found.

next_gate.name: KAMIL_CURATED_IMPACTITE_AU_PGE_MICROINCLUSION_AND_RAMESSIDE_TEXT_CORPUS_GATE
material_tasks: Locate published/sample-level analyses of Kamil dark-glass specimens L15, L05, L06, E30_m.s., MNA07_m.s. and related fallback deposits.
Search for measured Au, Pt, Ir, Pd, Ni and Co in individual glass clasts/blebs rather than inferring from bulk meteorite composition.
Flag any Au-rich inclusion only if concentration and morphology exceed the natural projectile-mixing baseline by a pre-registered threshold.
Prefer museum/university curated material and non-destructive imaging before any sampling.
text_tasks: Resolve the exact Kitchen 1975 Karnak passage cited as a probable meteorite description and recover its original Egyptian/transliteration/translation.
Build a dated corpus 1600-400 BCE for bjA-n-pt, meteors/shooting stars, sky-fire, impact/fall language, western/southern desert geography and extraordinary celestial events.
Separate royal similes and cosmological formulae from eyewitness/event-annal language.
Test whether any securely dated text independently localizes an event toward the southern/western desert rather than selecting texts after seeing Kamil.
